name: Champagne
officialRulesNote: Champagne AOC rules apply. This geometry comes through OpenDataWine access to INAO delimitation data.
commonPracticeNote: The same geographic delimitation is also used for Coteaux champenois in the OpenDataWine source, so the map renders the shared area once.

terroir.learningPoint: High latitude, cool climate, and chalk help Champagne retain high acidity for traditional-method sparkling wine.

structure: dry to sweet depending on dosage
tastingProfile.ageingPotential: moderate to high, especially vintage and prestige cuvées

name: Coteaux champenois
primaryStyle: Still dry red, white, and rosé
officialRulesNote: Coteaux champenois is a still-wine AOC. In the OpenDataWine source, it shares the same geometry as Champagne.
commonPracticeNote: Usually rare, still, and site/producer-specific; red examples are often Pinot Noir-led.

terroir.learningPoint: Use Coteaux champenois to remember that Champagne's delimited area also supports still wines, not only sparkling wine.

tastingProfile.ageingPotential: short to moderate, higher for top villages/producers

name: Rosé des Riceys
officialRulesNote: Rosé des Riceys is a distinct AOC for still rosé wine from the Les Riceys area.
commonPracticeNote: An important exam cue because it is Champagne-region wine, but not sparkling Champagne.

terroir.learningPoint: Rosé des Riceys is a rare still rosé AOC in the Côte des Bar, strongly associated with Pinot Noir.
